minutes.headline: Capital Planning Committee reviewed scoring and the requests list, and set four presentation dates in Nov–Dec.
minutes.summary: The committee went over the capital request list and the scoring criteria, which act as guidance and not a rule. It discussed how to weigh future-year items like Town Hall, TC Passos and Brooks House against the Municipal Building Committee's plans. It picked four meeting dates for department presentations; the only motion heard was adjournment.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair read the total of this year's capital requests across all departments.
A member asked for last year's final number and the answer was roughly that, affected by the tax situation.

budget_items.topic: Fire trucks and special purpose stabilization
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said fire trucks over four fiscal years total about the amount held in the special purpose stabilization account, with an article to spend part of it.

budget_items.topic: Municipal Building Committee Town Hall project cost
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said the cost is unknown but large, with ARPA money granted for engineering.
Cemetery requests would exceed the perpetual care funds available, which are not an enterprise fund.

budget_items.topic: Scoring points for grant funding and mandates
budget_items.what_was_said: Scoring awards the most points for a state or federal mandate and for available grant funding.

decisions.decision: Presentation meetings set for the 6th, 8th, 20th and 29th, 6 p.m. except the 20th at 7 p.m., at the Ritter building.
DPW, facilities and schools each get their own night; fire, police and library may be combined; schools placed on the 20th or 29th.
Departments will be asked to provide presentations in PowerPoint rather than PDF, ahead of the meeting.
The meetings will be recorded and made available through public access.
Schools to present later so the new facilities director can take part.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee set four department presentation meetings in Nov–Dec, with schools on the 20th or 29th and later so the new facilities director can join.
DPW, facilities and schools each get their own night; fire, police and library may be combined on one.
Members reviewed the capital request list and scoring criteria, which act as guidance rather than a rule; scoring gives the most points to mandates and available grant funding.
The committee discussed ranking future-year items such as Town Hall, TC Passos and Brooks House against the Municipal Building Committee's plans, and reached no resolution.
Departments will be asked to send PowerPoint rather than PDF presentations ahead of time, and the meetings will be recorded for public access.

why_it_matters: This committee ranks the capital requests that later reach Town Meeting as articles, so the scoring and the presentations shape which projects residents are asked to vote on and pay for.
The Town Hall project cost was described as unknown but large, and it was left unresolved, so how it fits beside other requests could affect future debt and tax bills.
